Haplotype P was found only in family members who suffered from cataract, and all family members who suffered from cataract had haplotype P.

quotes: The locus for the hereditary human Coppock-like cataract (CCL) is closely linked to a particular combination of polymorphic TaqI sites within the human gamma-crystallin gene cluster.
The CCL psi gamma E gene contains a cluster of sequence changes within and around its TATA box.

records.label: Seven-generation family with autosomal dominant pulverulent congenital cataract
quotes: The authors describe a seven-generation family with 48 of 138 individuals known to be affected with autosomal dominant congenital cataracts of the pulverulent type.
Twenty-eight of the 53 individuals examined had congenital cataracts. Of these patients, 19 eyes (8 right eyes and 11 left eyes) were unilateral and 9 were bilateral.

Severity of the cataracts included a subtle unilateral zonular cataract with 20/20 visual acuity, bilateral inner fetal nuclear pulverulent opacities with 20/16 visual acuity in both eyes, and dense unilateral and bilateral nuclear cataracts requiring early surgical removal.

quotes: Further analysis of the original Coppock-like-cataract family identified a missense mutation in a highly conserved segment of exon 2 of CRYGC. These mutations were not seen in a large control population.
we observed that the previously reported Coppock-like-cataract mutation, the first human cataract mutation, in the pseudogene CRYGE represented a polymorphism seen in 23% of our control population

quotes: DNA sequencing analysis of the CRYGA-D gene cluster of the affected members showed the heterozygous missense mutation c.502C>T in the CRYGC gene. This transition mutation resulted in the substitution of Arg at position 168 by Trp.
we described a family with nuclear congenital cataract that segregated the CRYGC missense mutation c.502C>T.
Analysis of the healthy members of the family and 170 unrelated controls showed a normal sequence of the CRYGA-D gene cluster.

records.label: Four-generation Chinese family
records.segregation: cosegregated with cataract in all affected members; absent in unaffected members and 100 controls
quotes: We investigated a four-generation Chinese family with six members affected with nuclear cataracts and microcornea.

The affected individuals presented with bilateral congenital nuclear cataracts that consisted of a central nuclear opacity affecting the embryonic, fetal, and infantile nucleus of the lens (Figure 2) and with congenital small eyeballs and corneas with a diameter of approximately 9–10 mm.
Every affected individual had the same poor visual acuity of hand movement in front of the eye, and they also had nystagmus and amblyopia.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

notes.statement: Guo et al. (2012) described a 4-generation Chinese family with isolated bilateral autosomal dominant nuclear cataracts and microcornea (corneal diameter approximately 9 mm); opacities involved the embryonic, fetal, and infantile nuclei, and all patients had nystagmus and amblyopia with normal intraocular pressure and no systemic abnormalities.
quotes: The nuclear opacities were located in the embryonic, fetal, and infantile nuclei. Bilateral nuclear cataracts and microcornea with a diameter of approximately 9 mm were consistent in all of the affected individuals.
Nystagmus and amblyopia were observed in all the patients. There was no history of other related systemic abnormalities in this family.

notes.statement: In affected members of a Chinese family with autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataract and microcornea, Guo et al. (2012) identified a c.471G>A transition (TGG-TGA) in exon 3 of the CRYGC gene, resulting in a trp157-to-ter (W157X) substitution predicted to truncate 18 C-terminal amino acids and disrupt the fourth Greek key motif. The mutation segregated with the disease and was not found in 100 controls.
quotes: Direct sequencing of the candidate gene cluster showed a c.471G>A transition in exon 3 of CRYGC, which co-segregated according to family members with cataracts, and was not observed in 100 normal controls.
Eighteen amino acids are truncated from the COOH-terminus of γC-crystallin as result of c.471G>A mutation.

notes.statement: Guo et al. (2012) noted that the same W157X protein change, resulting from a different nucleotide substitution (c.470G>A), had previously been reported in an unrelated Chinese family with a similar phenotype of nuclear cataract and microcornea, and concluded that W157X is disease-causing rather than a polymorphism.
quotes: The W157X mutation was not only observed in our family but also in another previously described family with nuclear cataracts and microcornea, indicating that W157X is the actual disease-causing mutation and should no longer be considered a single nucleotide polymorphism.
The previous W157X report was a c.470G>A transition and the clinical phenotype also was nuclear cataracts and microcornea. The phenotypes of these two mutations were similar.

notes.statement: Li et al. (2012) found that expression of the gamma-C-crystallin p.Gly129Cys mutant in zebrafish caused vacuoles and incomplete denucleation of the lens, recapitulating the human cataract phenotype.
quotes: Using zebrafish as a model, we demonstrated that γC-crystallin p.Gly129Cys mutant caused the vacuole and the incomplete denucleation of lens, recapitulating the cataract phenotype in human beings.

notes.statement: Li et al. (2012) showed by molecular modeling and spectroscopy that the G129C mutation impaired the tertiary structure of gamma-C-crystallin by modifying the H-bonding network in the C-terminal domain, dramatically decreased its thermal stability, and increased its propensity to aggregate under high concentration, heat, and UV irradiation stresses.
quotes: Molecular modeling and spectroscopic studies indicated that the mutation impaired the tertiary structure of the protein by modifying the H-bonding network in the C-terminal domain.

The mutation led to a dramatic decrease in the thermal stability of γC-crystallin, and a significant increase in the propensity of aggregation when subject to storage at high concentrations, heat, and UV- irradiation stresses.

notes.statement: Zhang et al. (2009) found linkage of autosomal dominant nuclear cataract with microcornea in a Chinese family to chromosome 2q32.3-q35, with a maximum 2-point lod score of 2.29 at marker D2S325 (theta = 0.0); haplotype analysis placed the locus in a 19.04-cM region between D2S117 and D2S2382 containing the gamma-crystallin gene cluster.
quotes: Evidence for linkage was detected at marker D2S325 (LOD score [Z]=2.29, recombination fraction [theta]=0.0), which closely flanks the gamma-crystallin gene cluster (CRYGA-CRYGD) on chromosome 2q32.3-q35.
The results of both linkage and haplotype analyses situated the disease gene in a 19.04 cM region bounded by D2S117 and D2S2382 at 2q32.3-q35.

notes.statement: Zhang et al. (2009) predicted that the CRYGC W157X mutation, affecting a highly conserved tryptophan, truncates 17 amino acids from the C terminus of gamma-C-crystallin, disrupting the fourth Greek key motif and possibly altering folding, stability and/or solubility.
quotes: The W157X mutation results in an in-frame stop codon at nucleotide 470 that leads to the truncation of 17 amino acids from the COOH-terminus of γC-crystallin.
The W157X mutation affects the Greek key motifs, and it is predicted to change the folding properties of γC-crystallin and/or affect its interactions with other crystallins.

notes.statement: Zhang et al. (2009) suggested that mutations disrupting lens biochemistry early in development may cause microphakia and secondary microcornea.
quotes: The association between microcornea and congenital cataracts in all affected individuals indicate that mutations disrupting lens biochemistry and physiology early in development can result in microphakia and subsequent microcornea as a secondary effect of damage to the lens.

notes.statement: Gonzalez-Huerta et al. (2007) noted that the CRYGC R168W mutation had previously been associated with lamellar cataract, whereas their family had nuclear congenital cataract. They described this as the first case of phenotypic heterogeneity in primary congenital cataract specifically associated with R168W.
quotes: This mutation has been associated with the phenotype of lamellar cataract but is also considered a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the NCBI database.
This is the first case of phenotypic heterogeneity in the primary congenital cataract specifically associated with the R168W mutation in the CRYGC gene.

notes.statement: Gonzalez-Huerta et al. (2007) did not find the c.502C>T variant in 170 unrelated controls. They concluded that R168W is the actual disease-causing mutation and should no longer be considered a SNP, as it was listed in the NCBI database.
quotes: Analysis of the healthy members of the family and 170 unrelated controls showed a normal sequence of the CRYGA-D gene cluster.
Our data and previous report support that R168W is the actual disease-causing mutation and should no longer be considered a SNP.

notes.statement: Santhiya et al. (2002) reported novel mutations in the gamma-crystallin genes that caused autosomal dominant congenital cataracts.
quotes: Novel mutations in the gamma-crystallin genes cause autosomal dominant congenital cataracts.

notes.statement: Ren et al. (2000) mapped the cataract in a seven-generation family to a 19-cM interval on chromosome 2q33-q35 that includes the gamma-crystallin gene cluster. The maximum lod score was 4.56 (theta = 0.02) with D2S157, and the lod score with CRYG was 3.57 (theta = 0.052).
quotes: We have localized the cataracts to a 19-cM interval on chromosome 2q33-q35 including the gamma-crystallin gene cluster. Maximum lod scores are 4.56 (theta=0.02) with D2S157, 3.66 (theta=0.12) with D2S72, and 3.57 (theta=0.052) with CRYG.

notes.statement: Ren et al. (2000) found that activation of the pseudo-gammaE-crystallin gene was unlikely to cause the cataracts in this family. Base changes in its TATA box were found in unaffected controls, so they could be excluded as a sole cause. The CRYGD gene showed no abnormalities.
quotes: Sequencing and allele-specific oligonucleotide analysis of the pseudo gammaE-crystallin promoter region from individuals in the pedigree suggest that activation of the gammaE-crystallin pseudo gene is unlikely to cause the cataracts in the family.
base changes in the TATA box but not the Sp1-binding site have been found in unaffected controls and can be excluded as a sole cause of cataracts.
The gammaD-crystallin gene shows no abnormalities

notes.statement: Ren et al. (2000) predicted that the CRYGC 5-bp duplication disrupts the reading frame and produces an unstable gamma-C-crystallin. This protein would contain 38 amino acids of the first Greek key motif followed by 52 random amino acids. They suggested that mutant beta-gamma-crystallins may not need to associate properly into oligomers to cause cataracts.
quotes: This mutation disrupts the reading frame of the gammaC-crystallin coding sequence and is predicted to result in the synthesis of an unstable gammaC-crystallin with 38 amino acids of the first "Greek key" motif followed by 52 random amino acids.
This finding suggests that the appropriate association of mutant betagamma-crystallins into oligomers is not necessary to cause cataracts

notes.statement: Héon et al. (1999) found that the change in the CRYGE pseudogene, reported earlier as the Coppock-like cataract mutation, was a polymorphism present in 23% of their control population. They noted that, to date, there was no direct evidence that up-regulation of a pseudogene causes cataracts.
quotes: we observed that the previously reported Coppock-like-cataract mutation, the first human cataract mutation, in the pseudogene CRYGE represented a polymorphism seen in 23% of our control population
There is no direct evidence, to date, that up-regulation of a pseudogene causes cataracts.

notes.statement: Héon et al. (1999) concluded that their findings were the first evidence that CRYGC is involved in human cataract formation.
quotes: To our knowledge, these findings are the first evidence of an involvement of CRYGC and support the role of CRYGD in human cataract formation.

notes.statement: Scott et al. (1994) studied a 7-generation family with autosomal dominant congenital pulverulent cataract in which the cataract appeared seemingly at random as either unilateral or bilateral. Including historic data, there were 48 affected members: 28 with unilateral cataract, 17 with bilateral cataract, and 3 obligate carriers who were not examined. In patients with unilateral cataract, detailed slit-lamp examination of the clinically unaffected eye showed no lens opacity.
quotes: Incorporating the historic data on patients who were not examined, we found 48 affected members (28 unilateral, 17 bilateral, 3 obligate carriers who were not examined).
The clinically unaffected eye in patients with unilateral cataracts showed no evidence of lenticular opacity under detailed slit-lamp examination.
The authors describe a large pedigree with the apparently random expression of an autosomal dominant gene as either unilateral or bilateral cataract.

notes.statement: Scott et al. (1994) reported that work was under way to determine whether the causative gene in their family was linked to previously defined cataract loci on chromosomes 1, 2, or 16.
quotes: Currently, work is under way to determine if the causative gene is linked to previously defined cataract loci on chromosomes 1, 2, or 16.

notes.statement: Brakenhoff et al. (1994) mapped the polymorphic TaqI sites closely linked to the hereditary Coppock-like cataract locus and found that they defined a 15-kb region encompassing the gamma-D and pseudo-gamma-E crystallin genes.
quotes: Mapping of these sites shows that they define a 15 kb region encompassing the gamma D and psi gamma E gene.

notes.statement: Brakenhoff et al. (1994) cloned the gamma-D and pseudo-gamma-E genes from the Coppock-like cataract chromosome. The gamma-D gene was functionally equivalent to the wildtype allele, whereas the pseudo-gamma-E gene had a cluster of sequence changes in and around its TATA box that together increased promoter activity 10-fold, raising its expression to 30% of that of gamma-D.
quotes: The gamma D gene was functionally equivalent to its allele cloned from a wild-type chromosome.
Together these cause a ten-fold increase in the activity of the psi gamma E promoter, raising the level of expression of this gene to 30% of that of the gamma D gene.

notes.statement: Brakenhoff et al. (1994) noted that the predicted protein product of the pseudo-gamma-E gene was a 6-kD N-terminal gamma-crystallin fragment. They suggested that reactivation of the pseudogene, with the resulting overexpression of this fragment, could be the cause of Coppock-like cataract.
quotes: The predicted protein product of the psi gamma E gene is a 6 kD N-terminal gamma-crystallin fragment.
Reactivation of the psi gamma E gene and concomitant overexpression of the gamma-crystallin fragment could be the cause of the Coppock-like cataract.

notes.statement: In a family with a hereditary Coppock-like cataract of the embryonic lens nucleus, Lubsen et al. (1987) found that the cataract locus was closely linked to the gamma-crystallin gene cluster. They reported a maximum lod score of 7.58 at theta = 0. They concluded that the primary cause of a human cataract could possibly be a lesion in a crystallin gene.
quotes: The absolute correlation between the presence of haplotype P and cataract within this family shows that the gamma-crystallin gene cluster and the locus for the Coppock-like cataract are closely linked [logarithm of odds (lod) score of 7.58 at its maximum at phi = 0].
This linkage provides genetic evidence that the primary cause of a cataract in humans could possibly be a lesion in a crystallin gene.

notes.statement: Lubsen et al. (1987) found that polymorphic TaqI sites in the gamma-crystallin gene cluster could define 8 possible haplotypes. Only 3 of these (Q, R, and S) were found in the Dutch and English population, and a fourth haplotype (P) was found in the family with cataract.
quotes: Together these restriction fragment length polymorphisms define eight possible haplotypes, three of which (Q, R, and S) were found in the Dutch and English population.
